Title: Monstera Deliciosa
Body (HTML):
The iconic Swiss Cheese Plant. Deep green, fenestrated leaves that can span 90cm across when mature — each new leaf more dramatic than the last. Native to the tropical forests of southern Mexico, this climbing aroid anchors any indoor jungle.

Why we love it: The moment a new leaf unfurls with its first fenestrations is pure plant-parent joy. Give it a moss pole and watch it climb.

Title: Fiddle Leaf Fig
Body (HTML):
The reigning icon of interior design. Huge violin-shaped leaves on a statuesque trunk — Ficus lyrata turns any corner into a focal point. A must-have for bright, airy spaces.

Why we love it: When this plant is happy, it rewards you with massive new leaves the size of dinner plates. The ultimate plant-parent flex.

Title: Snake Plant Laurentii
Body (HTML):
The undisputed champion of low-maintenance greenery. Dracaena trifasciata 'Laurentii' — sword-like leaves with golden-yellow margins that thrive on neglect. NASA-approved air purifier.

Why we love it: Travels well, survives offices, tolerates near-darkness, and looks sculptural doing it. The perfect first plant.

Title: ZZ Plant
Body (HTML):
Zamioculcas zamiifolia — glossy emerald leaves that look almost artificial, emerging from potato-like rhizomes that store water for weeks. Thrives in windowless bathrooms and dim offices.

Why we love it: Water it once a month. That's it. The plant that asks nothing and still looks like a million bucks.

Title: Golden Pothos
Body (HTML):
The cascade champion. Epipremnum aureum — heart-shaped leaves marbled with gold, trailing up to 3 meters. The fastest path to indoor jungle vibes in any room.

Why we love it: Propagates in a glass of water. Share cuttings with everyone you know. Watch it conquer your bookshelf.

Title: Peace Lily
Body (HTML):
Spathiphyllum — elegant white spathes rise like sails above glossy dark leaves. Nature's built-in water meter: when it droops dramatically, water it. Within hours, it's standing tall again.

Why we love it: The only low-light plant that also blooms. Plus it tells you exactly when it's thirsty — no guesswork.

Title: Philodendron Brasil
Body (HTML):
The collector's gateway philodendron — heart-shaped leaves streaked with electric lime variegation. Compact, fast-growing, and endlessly photographable on a shelf or in a hanging basket.

Why we love it: No two leaves are alike. Each new unfurl is a surprise — some nearly half-lime, others deep green with a single golden stripe.

Title: White Bird of Paradise
Body (HTML):
Strelitzia nicolai — banana-like leaves that can reach 2 meters indoors, creating an instant tropical atrium effect. The plant equivalent of a statement chandelier.

Why we love it: Those massive, paddle-shaped leaves transform any room into a luxury hotel lobby. Architectural, dramatic, unforgettable.

Title: Alocasia Polly
Body (HTML):
Amazonian Elephant Ear — dramatically arrow-shaped leaves with electric-white veins on deep jade green. Looks prehistoric, demands tropical humidity and bright filtered light.

Why we love it: Each new leaf is visibly bigger than the last. When humidity and warmth are right, this plant grows fast and looks unreal.

Title: Spider Plant
Body (HTML):
Chlorophytum comosum — the nostalgic favorite with arching ribbon-like leaves and cascading babies on long stems. The gift that keeps on giving, generation after generation.

Why we love it: Those baby plantlets. Pot them up, gift them, start a plant empire from a single mother plant. Pet-safe and air-purifying.

Title: Burgundy Rubber Plant
Body (HTML):
Ficus elastica 'Burgundy' — leaves the color of black cherry, each one emerging from a crimson sheath like a secret being revealed. A Victorian conservatory staple for the modern loft.

Why we love it: That moment when a new leaf unfurls from its bright red sheath. Never gets old. The deeper the burgundy, the happier the plant.

Title: Calathea Orbifolia
Body (HTML):
The diva of the Calathea world. Silver-green stripes radiate across round leaves the size of salad plates, which fold upward at night like praying hands. Absolutely stunning, absolutely demanding.

Why we love it: When you nail the humidity and distilled-water routine, the foliage payoff is unmatched. A living piece of art.

Title: Chinese Money Plant
Body (HTML):
Pilea peperomioides — pancake-flat circular leaves on delicate stems, a symbol of prosperity and friendship. Passed from friend to friend for generations, it's the original social-media plant.

Why we love it: Constantly produces pups (baby plants) around its base. Pop them out, pot them up, and you have gifts for everyone you know.

Title: Jade Plant
Body (HTML):
Crassula ovata — thick, fleshy oval leaves on a bonsai-like trunk. A symbol of good luck and prosperity, this succulent can live for decades, passed down through generations.

Why we love it: With enough light, the leaf edges blush a soft red. It thrives on neglect and looks better with age — the definition of a legacy plant.

Title: String of Pearls
Body (HTML):
Senecio rowleyanus — perfectly spherical green beads cascade from a hanging pot like a living beaded curtain. The most photogenic trailing plant in existence.

Why we love it: Those perfect little peas. Each one is a modified leaf storing water — nature's engineering at its most elegant. Drape it high and watch it flow.

Title: Anthurium Red Flamingo
Body (HTML):
Anthurium andraeanum — glossy heart-shaped red spathes with a curling yellow spadix, hovering above dark green leaves. Blooms last for months, making it the longest-flowering houseplant.

Why we love it: Those waxy red blooms look almost fake — people will touch them to check. Each one lasts 8-12 weeks. A perpetual valentine.

Title: Hoya Krimson Queen
Body (HTML):
Hoya carnosa 'Krimson Queen' — thick waxy leaves edged in cream and pink, growing on long twining vines. Produces clusters of star-shaped pink flowers that smell like chocolate at night.

Why we love it: The pink new growth, the porcelain-like flowers, the chocolate fragrance. This plant is a sensory experience wrapped in a trailing vine.

Title: Dracaena Song of India
Body (HTML):
Dracaena reflexa 'Song of India' — narrow, lance-shaped leaves striped in chartreuse and cream, radiating from sculptural stems. A living sculpture that thrives on filtered light.

Why we love it: The architectural silhouette. Each stem is a vertical accent, and the variegation catches light like stained glass. Low-maintenance elegance.

Title: Philodendron Pink Princess
Body (HTML):
The crown jewel of philodendron collecting. Deep burgundy-black leaves splashed with bubblegum pink variegation — no two leaves the same, every new unfurl a lottery ticket.

Why we love it: The pink. That impossible, vivid, Barbie-dream-house pink, emerging from leaves so dark they're almost black. The most Instagrammable plant alive.

Title: Aloe Vera
Body (HTML):
Aloe barbadensis miller — the original medicinal plant, with fleshy serrated leaves filled with cooling gel. A kitchen windowsill essential for burns, cuts, and skincare routines.

Why we love it: Snap off a leaf, squeeze out the gel, and soothe a sunburn instantly. Beauty, utility, and nearly impossible to kill — the original multitasker.

Title: Monstera Thai Constellation
Body (HTML):
The holy grail of Monstera collecting. Genetically stable cream-and-green variegation creates a constellation map across each leaf — a living piece of botanical art that holds its value.

Why we love it: Tissue-cultured for stable variegation — no reverting to solid green. Each leaf is a permanent celestial map, and the plant appreciates in value as it grows.

Title: Boston Fern
Body (HTML):
Nephrolepis exaltata — the classic Victorian parlor fern with cascading feather-like fronds. A humidity-loving shower plant that transforms bathrooms into tropical retreats.

Why we love it: That lush, feathery volume. Hang it in a bathroom with a window and watch it explode into a fountain of green. The ultimate shower plant.

Title: Staghorn Fern
Body (HTML):
Platycerium bifurcatum — antler-shaped fronds that mount on wooden boards like living wall art. An epiphyte that grows on trees in nature, needing no soil — just humidity and bright indirect light.

Why we love it: Mount it on a board, hang it on the wall. It's a living sculpture that breaks every rule about what a houseplant should look like. Conversation starter guaranteed.

Title: Fishbone Cactus
Body (HTML):
Epiphyllum anguliger — zigzag leaves that look like fishbones, cascading from a hanging pot. Produces enormous fragrant white flowers that bloom for a single magical night.

Why we love it: The silhouette. Those cartoonish zigzag leaves are pure whimsy. And when it blooms — a hand-sized white flower that fills the room with vanilla fragrance at midnight.
